Force and Translational Dynamics: Newton's first law
An object maintains its motion unless acted on by a net force
Inertial mass
The measure of an object's resistance to acceleration
Newton's second law
Acceleration equals net force divided by mass
Newton's third law
Forces come in equal and opposite pairs acting on different objects
Free-body diagram
A diagram showing every force acting on a single object
Normal force
The perpendicular support force from a surface
Static friction
Friction preventing motion from starting, up to a maximum value
Kinetic friction
Friction acting on a sliding object, generally constant
Coefficient of friction
The ratio describing how rough a surface pair is
Tension
The pulling force transmitted along a rope or cable
Inclined plane analysis
Resolving weight into components along and perpendicular to a slope
Translational equilibrium
The condition of zero net force and zero acceleration
Centripetal force
The net inward force required for circular motion
Gravitational field strength

Work, Energy, and Power: Work
Force times displacement in the direction of the force
Work by a variable force
The area under a force versus displacement graph
Kinetic energy
Energy of motion, one half mass times velocity squared
Gravitational potential energy
Stored energy from position in a gravitational field
Elastic potential energy
Energy stored in a stretched or compressed spring
Hooke's law
Spring force proportional to displacement from equilibrium
Spring constant
The stiffness value k of a spring
Work-energy theorem
Net work equals the change in kinetic energy
Conservation of mechanical energy
Total mechanical energy constant when only conservative forces act
Conservative force
A force whose work is path independent, such as gravity
Nonconservative force
A force such as friction that dissipates mechanical energy
Power
The rate at which work is done, in watts
Energy bar chart
A representation tracking energy transfers within a system
Linear Momentum: Linear momentum
Mass times velocity, a vector quantity
Impulse
Force applied over time, equal to the change in momentum
Impulse-momentum theorem
Net impulse equals the resulting change in momentum
Conservation of momentum
Total momentum constant when net external force is zero
Elastic collision
A collision conserving both momentum and kinetic energy
Inelastic collision
A collision conserving momentum while losing kinetic energy
Perfectly inelastic collision
A collision in which objects move together afterward
Centre of mass
The mass-weighted average position of a system
Internal versus external forces
Internal forces cancel in a system; only external forces change total momentum
Force versus time graph
Its area under the curve gives impulse
Two-dimensional collision
A collision analysed by conserving momentum along each axis separately

The rotational effect of a force, force times lever arm
Lever arm
The perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of action
Rotational equilibrium
The condition of zero net torque
Moment of inertia

Angular displacement
The angle through which an object rotates
Angular velocity
The rate of change of angular position
Angular acceleration

Rolling without slipping

Tangential acceleration
Linear acceleration of a point on a rotating body

Centre of gravity
The point where an object's weight can be treated as acting
